<entry id="M01035">

<entry id="M01036">
<head-word>מַטָּעָה</head-word>
<head-word>מַטַּעַת</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> 1) same.</definition>
<notes> f. </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> same. Gen. R. s. 15, beg.; Midr. Till. to Ps. CIV, 16 ישבעון מַטָּעֲתָן they (the cedars) shall enjoy their transplantation.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 30 מַטָּעַת כרמים plantation of vineyards. Cant. R. to II, 3 כמטעת של כרם (prob. כמַטָּעוֹת pl.) like the rows of plants in a vineyard. Midr. Sam. ch. XXVIII מַטָּעָתָךְ מהיכן היא whence is thy origin?</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>cultivated state</italic>, opp. חורבן.</definition>
<notes> Y. Kil. IV, end, 29
<sup>c</sup> יותר ממַטָּעָתוֹ more than when it is cultivated. Midr. Sam. ch. XXV שהיה רואה מטעת שלו נקצצת וכ' he saw his (Saul’s) plantation cut down (his descendants put to death, v. II Sam. ch. XXI), and did not worry about it &c.; Yalk. Ps. 765 מעיל (corr. acc.).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<pos> f.</pos>

<xref rid="I00637"> טָפַח II)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>towel, apron</italic> (for wiping moist hands); in gen. 
<italic>bandage, wrap</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tosef. Ḥag. III, 2 מַטְפַּחתּוֹ his apron; Ḥag. II, 7. Kel. XXIV, 14 (מ') של ידים towel, של ספרים bands for scrolls; של תכריך bands around shrouds; ושל נבלי בני לוי and the wraps of the musical instruments of the Levites (Maim.); (oth. vers. של תכריך נבלי וכ' bands used for tying up the instruments &c.). Ib. XXVIII, 5 כסת שעשאה מ' a bag of a bolster which was changed into a plain sheet; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. מִטְפָּחוֹת</plural-form>. Ib. XXIV, 14 שלש מ' הן וכ' there are three kinds of 
<italic>mitpa</italic>
<italic>ḥ</italic>
<italic>oth</italic>, v. supra. Snh. 100
<sup>a</sup> (in Chald. dict.) מתקני מִטְפְּחוֹת ספרים בי רבי וכ' Ms. M. were fitting up wraps for the books in the house of &c. Kil. IX, 3; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="M01052">

<italic>sing</italic>.).—Taan. 9

<italic>womb</italic>, v. מִיטְרִין.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<pos> m.</pos>

<definition> (טְרַד; cmp. Arab.</definition>
<notes>
<italic>mitrad</italic>, hasta brevis) 
<italic>the hunter’s spear</italic>. Targ. Y. II Gen. XXXVI, 39 (play on מטרד, ib.) גברא דהוה לעי במ' וכ' (‘Rashi’ to Gen. R. s. 83 quotes: גברא טָרוֹדָא דהוה לעולם כמטרידא, read: לעי במ') a (busy) man, for all his life-time he worked with the hunting spear; Y. I במ' ובסרדיתא with hunting spear and with net; Targ. I Chr. I, 50 במִטְרְדוּתָא ובסרדותא.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="M01055">
<head-word>מטְרוֹנָא</head-word>
<head-word>מַטְרוֹנָה</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (matrona) 
<italic>matron, lady</italic> (mostly used of Roman women of quality).</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 41, beg., a. e., v. טוֹלְמִיסִין. Ib. s. 52 עשאה מ' he raised her to the rank of a lady (who is protected from the gaze of men, v. כָּסָה II). Ex. R. s. 44 נטלה … ועשאה מ' וכ' he took her for wife and made her a lady and gave her a chain &c. Gen. R. s. 4; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. מַטְרוֹנוֹת, מַטְרוֹנִיּוֹת,</plural-form> v. next w.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="M01056">
<head-word>מַטְרוֹנִית</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (preced.) 
<italic>lady-like</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ex. R. s. 3 שפחה אחת מ' a maid, opp. כושית a negress (slave). In gen. 
<italic>lady</italic>. Num. R. s. 16 (not מטרוניתא); a. e.—
<plural-form>Pl. מַטְרוֹנִיּוֹת</plural-form>. Y. Ned. III, end, 38
<sup>b</sup> משל לשתי מטרניות וכ' (not לשני) this is to be compared to two ladies meeting one another (in carriages). 
<pgbrk id="pg770" />Ex. R. s. 19 שתי מַטְרוֹנוֹת דומות ed. Wil. (oth. ed. … ניות) two ladies apparently of equal rank. Sifré Deut. 317 (ref. to Deut. XXXII, 14 ‘with the fat of’ &c.) אלו מ' שלהם this alludes to their (the Roman) ladies (living in luxury); a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<plural-form>Pl. מַטְרוֹנְיָתָא</plural-form>. Targ. Esth. II, 14 (not … נֵי'; h. text פלגשים). Targ. II Chr. XXXV, 25 (h. text שָׁרוֹת!).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

Gen. R. s. 92 מטרפ' היתה וכ' it was a metropolis and you say, ‘they returned to the town’!; a. fr.—[Gen. R. s. 42, v. אֱלֶיוְתְּרוֹפּוֹלִיס.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<italic>a solution of acorns</italic>; also 
<italic>a solution of gall-nuts</italic>. Gitt. 19
<sup>a</sup> (v. אֲפַץ) שאין מי מ' על גבי מי מ' (Ar. ע"ג מ') for a tanned ink will not take on a tanned hide. Y. ib. II, 44

VI, 1 שלשה מ' אסורין וכ' three kinds of prohibitions exist with reference to the nazarite.—שבעת המ' the seven products of Palestine (Deut. VIII, 8). Bicc. III, 6; a. fr.—כְּמִין
